description: A Kuching-based team of innovators building an interactive lunar outpost game for the next generation of explorers. We are transforming complex space engineering trade-offs balancing power, life support, radiation shielding, and food production into an intuitive, high-stakes experience where young learners discover firsthand what makes a deep-space mission succeed or fail.
summary: We propose AstroBorneo: Mission Survival Academy, a visual-first educational Moon-base game designed for children aged 7–12. The game aims to let young players explore an interactive lunar base, tap buildings, and answer picture-based pop-up challenges. Across five planned mission cycles, players would manage power, air, water, food, and crew safety while responding to energy shortages, equipment problems, and space-weather scenarios. Clear icons, animations, and visual feedback are intended to make the game accessible even to children with limited reading skills. Inspired by real space-engineering concepts and drawing on NASA scientific resources where feasible, AstroBorneo aims to make learning about life on the Moon engaging and fun.
details:
AstroBorneo: Mission Survival Academy

Project Details

AstroBorneo: Mission Survival Academy is an interactive, visual-first Moon-base survival game designed for children aged 7–12. Players explore a lunar base, complete picture-based challenges, and make engineering decisions to keep astronauts safe. Through resource management, mission events, and NASA scientific resources, AstroBorneo transforms complex space-survival concepts into a fun, accessible STEM learning experience.

The following are the main features driving the application:

Interactive Moon Base Exploration

Players explore a Moon base featuring six interactive facilities: Solar Power, Greenhouse, Habitat, Water Recycler, Radiation Shield, and Communications. Each facility offers a visual mini-game where players solve problems and maintain essential systems.

Mission Survival & Resource Management

Players manage five essential resources: Power, Air, Water, Food, and Crew Safety. A five-cycle mission simulation challenges them to balance limited resources while responding to reduced solar power, equipment failures, and radiation events. Players experience engineering trade-offs and observe how their decisions affect resources and mission outcomes.

Visual Challenges & Learning

Picture-based mini-games, colorful icons, animations, and immediate feedback are designed to make learning more accessible to young players. Interactive challenges and science quizzes help children understand how their decisions affect astronaut survival.

NASA Scientific Data Integration

AstroBorneo incorporates NASA scientific resources to connect gameplay concepts with real space science:

  • NASA DONKI: Real solar flare and space-weather observations.
  • NASA RadLab: ISS radiation measurements supporting radiation-safety education.
  • NASA OSDR: Space biology research (OSD-314) supporting greenhouse and plant-growth education.

NASA observations are presented as scientific references, while resource consumption, mission events, and survival outcomes are based on simplified game simulations.

Use Cases for AstroBorneo

STEM Education & Independent Learning

User: Children aged 7–12.

Scenario: A child explores a Moon base, completes interactive facility challenges, and learns how power shortages, oxygen production, water recycling, and radiation protection affect astronaut survival.

Classroom & Group Learning

User: Teachers, schools, and STEM educators.

Scenario: Teachers use the five-cycle mission simulation to demonstrate real engineering trade-offs. Students compare decisions, observe resource changes, and discuss strategies for maintaining a sustainable lunar outpost.

Technical Explanation

Project Architecture

Frontend:

Built with React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, and Vite. Features an interactive lunar environment, animated astronauts, visual mini-games, resource indicators, and responsive interfaces.

Backend:

Powered by Express.js (Node.js), managing NASA API requests, data validation, caching, and communication between the frontend and NASA services.

NASA Data Integration:

Retrieves NASA DONKI space-weather observations and NASA RadLab ISS radiation measurements when available, while referencing NASA OSDR-314 space biology research. Archived NASA data provides fallback support when live API requests are unavailable.

Game Simulation Engine:

A TypeScript-based simulation engine calculates resource consumption, system performance, mission events, and survival outcomes. The five-cycle mission simulator and interactive Moon-base survival mode provide complementary learning experiences.

Educational Design:

Uses visual interaction, short instructions, mini-games, science quizzes, and immediate feedback to simplify complex space-engineering concepts for children.

Data Management:

Uses local browser storage for game progress, mission history, and scores. NASA API caching and historical-data fallbacks support continued educational gameplay when external data is unavailable.

Scalability & Extensibility：

AstroBorneo is built as a browser-based educational game with responsive layouts and touch controls, designed for use on computers, tablets, and smartphones without additional software installation.

Beyond its current single-player lunar survival experience, AstroBorneo has the potential to evolve into an expandable STEM learning platform. Future developments include adaptive difficulty levels tailored to different ages and learning abilities, cooperative multiplayer missions where players collaborate as astronauts and engineers, and multilingual voice assistance to improve accessibility.

The lunar map could expand with new facilities, exploration areas, and interactive challenges, introducing different gameplay modes and increasingly complex engineering decisions. Further NASA dataset integration could introduce changing mission conditions, while an expanded educator dashboard could help teachers monitor classroom learning progress and assess students' problem-solving skills.

These improvements would allow AstroBorneo to grow from an educational prototype into a collaborative, accessible, cross-platform, and data-driven STEM learning experience.
